8:
SAY:
- "Today we need a pencil, a mini whiteboard with a texta, and our booklet."
- "Put them on your desk."

DO:
- Hold up each item.
- Wait until each student has them ready.

TEACHER NOTES:
Quick setup. Keep under 30 seconds.

WATCH FOR:
- Students still searching when teaching starts. Pause and reset.
9:
TEACHER NOTES:
Section divider for the shared read aloud. Move on quickly.
10:
SAY:
- "Today we are going to read Fang Fang's Chinese New Year again."
- "Listen for how Fang Fang feels at the start and at the end."
- "Our big question is: why do you think Fang Fang did not want to invite Lisa at first, but was happy at the end?"

DO:
- Read pages 1 to 22 aloud.
- Pause at the suggested points.
- After page 3 'it's silly', ask 'Why was Fang Fang nervous to invite Lisa?'
- After page 7 'little surprised', ask 'How did Fang Fang feel when her family spoke in Chinese?'
- After page 11 'like it!', ask 'How did Lisa respond to the duck and fish?'
- After page 14 'a laugh', ask 'What did Lisa do with chopsticks?'
- After page 22 'fantastic!', ask 'What does this story show us about trying new things?'
- After page 22 'that too!', ask 'Why did Fang Fang feel proud at the end?'
- After page 22 'Fang Fang', ask 'What did you learn from this book?'

TEACHER NOTES:
Third and final read of the storybook. The focus is abstract reasoning. Anticipated answers to the guiding question: she was worried Lisa would not understand or like the food, but Lisa tried everything; sharing her culture made Fang Fang proud.

WATCH FOR:
- Students stuck on the literal level. Push for 'why' answers, not just 'what happened'.
11:
TEACHER NOTES:
Section divider for vocabulary. The focus word is 'tease'. Move on to the routine slide.
12:
SOURCES:
Collins Secondary School Dictionary, https://schools.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/secondary/adapted, accessed 10.02.26

SAY:
- "Our word today is tease."
- "Say it with me. Tease."
- "Tease means to bother someone on purpose to get a reaction."
- "In the story, the boy teased the lion with a ball."
- "The boy teased his brother by running away with his ice cream."

DO:
- Point to the word.
- Have students choral say it three times.
- Make a 'pretend hold something away' action when you say tease.

TEACHER NOTES:
Follow the four-part vocabulary routine. 'Tease' has both playful and unkind meanings, so the next slides unpack the difference.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who only know the unkind meaning. Reassure them tease can also be playful.
13:
SAY:
- "In the story, the boy teased the lion with a ball."
- "Ask: was he kindly sharing the ball? Expected: no."
- "Ask: was he holding it close, moving it around to get a reaction? Expected: yes."
- "A reaction is what you do or how you feel after something happens."

DO:
- Read the slide aloud.
- Mime the action of holding something close and moving it.
- Take a quick choral response on each question.

TEACHER NOTES:
This slide unpacks 'tease' through the lion example. The new word 'reaction' is also defined. Foundation students may need that defined again with an example.

WATCH FOR:
- Students confusing 'tease' with 'help'. Use the action to show the difference.
14:
SAY:
- "I will read three questions. You answer yes or no."
- "Ask: does teasing mean helping someone? Expected: no."
- "Ask: does teasing try to get a reaction? Expected: yes."
- "Ask: can teasing sometimes hurt feelings? Expected: yes."

DO:
- Read each question one at a time.
- Cue thumbs after each.
- Affirm both 'yes' answers and the 'no' answer.

TEACHER NOTES:
Three-question check. Each angle of meaning is targeted. If students struggle with the third, briefly discuss kind versus unkind teasing.

WATCH FOR:
- Students saying teasing is always kind or always mean. Affirm both can happen.
15:
SAY:
- "Listen to this story."
- "On his birthday, Mia held her brother's present behind her back and said, 'Oh no, I think I forgot your gift!'"
- "He looked worried for a second. She laughed and handed him the brightly wrapped box."
- "They both smiled."
- "Ask: was Mia's tease kind or unkind? Expected: kind, playful."

DO:
- Read the short story aloud with expression.
- Take a quick partner share.
- Ask one student why this tease was playful.

TEACHER NOTES:
This story models playful teasing. Foundation students need explicit examples of playful versus unkind teasing.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who think Mia was unkind. Re-read the ending where they both smile.
16:
SAY:
- "Look at the picture. The sister is holding her brother's hat up high so he cannot reach it."
- "Ask: how is she teasing her brother? Expected: keeping the hat away from him to get a reaction."
- "Show me on your whiteboard or tell your partner."

DO:
- Read the slide aloud.
- Take a partner share.
- Take one or two responses.

CFU CHECKPOINT:
Technique: Pair Share, then Cold Call
Script:
- Ask: how is the sister teasing her brother? Expected: keeping the hat out of reach to get a reaction.
- Scan for: pairs talking, then a clear answer when called.
PROCEED:
- Most students give a relevant answer. Move on.
PIVOT:
- Most likely: students name something not in the picture.
- Reteach: point to the hat held up high in the picture.
- Re-check: ask 'why is she holding the hat up?' Expected: so he cannot reach it.

TEACHER NOTES:
This slide is a CFU. Use it to confirm students can describe a tease in their own words.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who freeze. Whisper-prompt by pointing to the picture.
17:
SAY:
- "Complete the sentence: I do not like when people tease me because..."
- "Tell your partner why."
- "Ask: a possible answer? Expected: I think they are trying to annoy me, it hurts my feelings."

DO:
- Read the slide aloud.
- Pair share.
- Take 1 to 2 responses.
- Affirm feelings.

SENSITIVITY ADVISORY:
- What it is: Some students may have experienced unkind teasing.
- Framing language: "It is okay to feel sad if someone teases you in a way that hurts."
- Watch for: Students who go quiet or look upset.
- Protocol: Affirm their feelings. Remind students that kind teasing is when both people are smiling.

TEACHER NOTES:
Keep the discussion short and warm. Foundation students may share strong personal feelings.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who share a recent unkind moment. Acknowledge briefly and follow up privately if needed.
18:
SAY:
- "Teasing means..."
- "Ask: A, having fun, or B, bothering someone on purpose? Expected: B, bothering someone on purpose."
- "Show me on your fingers, A or B."

DO:
- Cover the answer.
- Reveal.
- Have students choral say 'tease means to bother someone on purpose'.

CFU CHECKPOINT:
Technique: Show Me Fingers
Script:
- Ask: which is the meaning of tease, A having fun, or B bothering someone on purpose? Expected: B.
- Scan for: most fingers showing B.
PROCEED:
- >=80% show B. Move to recount work.
PIVOT:
- Most likely: students pick A because some teasing is playful.
- Reteach: tell them tease always means to bother on purpose, but sometimes it is gentle.
- Re-check: ask 'is teasing about getting a reaction?' Expected: yes.

TEACHER NOTES:
Threshold check. The dictionary meaning is 'to bother on purpose to get a reaction'. Playful or unkind, the bothering is the key part.

WATCH FOR:
- Students with mixed fingers. Take one of each and ask 'why?'
19:
TEACHER NOTES:
Section divider for understanding, responding to and creating text. The next slides build the final sentence of a recount.
20:
SAY:
- "Let's listen to the recount about Chinese New Year again."
- "Listen for the very last sentence."

DO:
- Read the mentor recount aloud (Last week, we went to Chinatown... I felt proud and happy).
- Pause briefly between each part.
- End on the final sentence.

TEACHER NOTES:
Existing note: re-read the recount. Quick I Do for the new focus on the final sentence.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who jump in with details. Tell them to listen for the last sentence today.
21:
SAY:
- "The final sentence is: I felt proud and happy because it was a special celebration with my family."
- "The final sentence tells the reader how you felt."
- "It finishes the recount."
- "It also tells us why the celebration was important."

DO:
- Read the slide aloud.
- Point to 'final sentence'.
- Use the feeling icon action (hand on heart).

TEACHER NOTES:
Existing note: highlight the final sentence and explain its job. Connect to the feeling icon from Lesson 1.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who think the final sentence is just another event. Show that it tells about how you felt.
22:
SAY:
- "Look at the final sentence again."
- "I felt proud and happy because it was a special celebration with my family."
- "Ask: what is the feeling? Expected: proud and happy."
- "This sentence uses 'because' to tell us why."

DO:
- Read the slide aloud.
- Have students do the hand-on-heart action when they say 'proud and happy'.
- Underline or point to 'because'.

TEACHER NOTES:
Existing note: identify the feeling and the use of 'because'. Foundation students may not have used 'because' to explain. Model it.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who name a different feeling. Bring them back to 'proud and happy' from the sentence.
23:
SAY:
- "Let's look at our other recount about the birthday at the beach."
- "I will read the whole recount so far."
- "On my last birthday, my family and I went to the beach."
- "First, I played cricket with my family on the sand."
- "Then, my brother and I went swimming in the ocean."
- "After that, we shared and ate lots of yummy food."
- "Now we need a final sentence."

DO:
- Read the recount aloud, with feeling.
- Use the icon actions for opening, detail and feeling.
- Promise students they will help create the final sentence.

TEACHER NOTES:
Existing note: briefly recap the modelled celebration. Set up the next slide where students help build the final sentence.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who try to add a fourth event. Tell them this recount is finished and we are adding the feeling now.
24:
SAY:
- "What could the feeling be at the end of this celebration?"
- "It made me feel...?"
- "Ask: name a feeling word. Expected: happy, loved, lucky, special."
- "Show me with your hand on your heart."

DO:
- Read the slide aloud.
- Brainstorm feelings with the class.
- Add a few more student suggestions to the list.

TEACHER NOTES:
Existing note: brainstorm different feelings. Build a class list. Foundation students may need to be reminded these are feelings, not events.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who say events instead of feelings. Use the heart action and ask 'how did you feel?'
25:
SAY:
- "Listen to this final sentence."
- "It made me feel special because I spent time with my family at my favourite place."
- "Ask: what is the feeling? Expected: special."
- "Ask: why? Expected: spent time with family at favourite place."

DO:
- Read the slide aloud.
- Use the heart action.
- Highlight 'because' in the sentence.

TEACHER NOTES:
We Do for a modelled final sentence. Foundation students should hear feeling + because + reason.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who only repeat the feeling. Push them to also say the reason.
26:
SAY:
- "Now let's read the whole recount."
- "On my last birthday, my family and I went to the beach."
- "First, I played cricket with my family on the sand."
- "Then, my brother and I went swimming in the ocean."
- "After that, we shared and ate lots of yummy food."
- "It made me feel special because I spent time with my family at my favourite place."

DO:
- Read the full recount aloud, with strong expression.
- Use the icon actions for each part.
- Choral read the final sentence with the class.

TEACHER NOTES:
Existing note: say the full recount aloud so students hear how the last sentence finishes the recount. This is the model students will replicate in their You Do.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who join in confidently. They are ready for the You Do.
- Students who are silent. Stand near them and prompt the icon actions.
27:
SAY:
- "Listen to two final sentences."
- "I felt happy."
- "I loved my celebration because I got to do lots of my favourite things, which made me feel happy."
- "Ask: which is better? Expected: the second one."
- "Ask: why? Expected: it tells more, gives a reason."

DO:
- Read both sentences.
- Take responses on whiteboards or fingers.
- Reveal the answer and explain.

CFU CHECKPOINT:
Technique: Show Me Fingers
Script:
- Ask: which is a better final sentence, one or two? Expected: 2.
- Scan for: most fingers showing 2.
PROCEED:
- >=80% show 2. Move to the You Do.
PIVOT:
- Most likely: students pick the shorter sentence because it is easier.
- Reteach: read the second sentence again and point out it has both feeling and reason.
- Re-check: ask 'which one tells us why?' Expected: the second one.

TEACHER NOTES:
Threshold check before the You Do.

WATCH FOR:
- Students with mixed fingers. Take one of each and ask 'why?'
28:
SAY:
- "Find your celebration drawings from before."
- "Practise saying your recount to a partner."
- "Use your opening sentence and your detail sentences."
- "Point to each picture as you say the parts."

DO:
- Pair students up.
- Listen in to a few pairs.
- Praise students who use the time connectives.

TEACHER NOTES:
Warm-up rehearsal before adding the final sentence.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who skip the time connectives. Whisper-prompt them.
29:
SAY:
- "Now you will create a final sentence for your celebration."
- "Remember, it tells how you felt and gives a reason."
- "Use these starters if you need: It made me feel..., I loved..., I felt..., I loved my celebration because..."

DO:
- Read each sentence starter aloud.
- Have students think silently for 30 seconds.
- Listen in to a few partner shares.

TEACHER NOTES:
This is the You Do for the final sentence. Use the sentence starters to scaffold students who freeze.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who only say a feeling. Prompt for 'because...'
30:
SAY:
- "Find the booklet page for your final sentence."
- "Draw a picture to match your final sentence."
- "Make sure your picture shows how you felt."

DO:
- Direct students to the booklet.
- Walk around and prompt for feeling details.
- Affirm faces showing different feelings.

TEACHER NOTES:
This is the You Do drawing for the final sentence. Foundation students often draw a smiley face. Push them to show their feeling clearly.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who freeze. Prompt 'how did you feel? Show that on the face.'
31:
SAY:
- "Now tell your whole recount to a partner."
- "Use your pictures and icons to help you."
- "Use actions as you say each part."

DO:
- Pair students up.
- Listen in.
- Invite a few students to share with the class.
- Praise students who include all three parts (opening, details, final).

ENABLING & EXTENDING:
ENABLING PROMPT:
- Task: Provide sentence frames (I loved my celebration because ___). Stand near the student and prompt each part.
EXTENDING PROMPT:
- Task: Encourage the student to use simple actions or gestures as they retell, to support expression.

TEACHER NOTES:
Existing note: students tell the whole recount. This is the readiness signal for Lesson 8 (presentation).

WATCH FOR:
- Students who can confidently retell with opening, details, and final. They are ready for Lesson 8.
- Students still missing one part. Plan a quick re-teach in Lesson 8.
32:
TEACHER NOTES:
Closing credits slide. No teaching needed. Save the celebration drawings for Lesson 8 (oral presentation).
